beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you again.
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, we met robots. We learned that robots follow algorithms, they don't have feelings, and they love doing the same job again and again.
beats.caption: Last time: robots follow algorithms

beats.vo: Today is chapter four of our unit, Computers in Our World. It's called, Data. What computers remember.
beats.caption: Chapter 4 · Data — What Computers Remember

beats.vo: Have you ever wondered how a game remembers your high score, even after you switch it off? Hmm. Let's find out!
beats.caption: How does a game remember your score?

beats.vo: Meet Aarav. Aarav loves playing a cricket game on his tablet.
beats.caption: Meet Aarav, the cricket game fan

beats.vo: One evening, he smashes a six, and then another one! Fifty two runs. His best score ever!
beats.caption: 52 runs! His best score ever!

beats.vo: Then mum calls, dinner's ready! So Aarav switches the tablet off, and runs to eat.
beats.caption: Dinner time! Tablet switched off

beats.vo: The next morning, he opens the game again. And it says, welcome back, Aarav! High score, fifty two.
beats.caption: "Welcome back, Aarav! High score: 52"

beats.vo: But the tablet was off all night. So how did the game remember his name, and his score? Think about it.
beats.caption: How did the game remember? Think!

beats.vo: Here's the secret. Before Aarav switched it off, the game saved those facts. It stored them safely inside the tablet, a bit like writing them in a notebook.
beats.caption: The game saved the facts, like a notebook

beats.vo: Those facts a computer keeps have a special name. They're called data.
beats.caption: Those saved facts are called DATA

beats.vo: Data is the facts a computer stores. Things like names, scores, and photos.
beats.caption: Data = facts a computer stores

beats.vo: So Aarav's name is data. His score of fifty two is data. Even his little player picture is data. A computer remembers things by storing data.
beats.caption: Name · Score · Picture → all data!

beats.vo: And once you start looking, you'll find data everywhere!
beats.caption: Data is everywhere!

beats.vo: Your name and your class are data. The marks on your test are data. The score in a game, and the nickname you pick, are data too.
beats.caption: Name · Class · Marks · Score · Nickname

beats.vo: What about a photo you click on a tablet? Yes! That's data too. The tablet stores every tiny dot of colour, so it can show you the picture later.
beats.caption: A photo saved on a tablet is data too!

beats.vo: Now, let's peek into your school office. The school computer stores lots of data about every student.
beats.caption: What does a school computer store?

beats.vo: It stores students' names, and roll numbers. It stores marks in each test. And parents' phone numbers, so the teacher can call home.
beats.caption: Names · Roll numbers · Marks · Phone numbers

beats.vo: But can it store the taste of your tiffin? Or how the wind feels today? No! Those are feelings, not facts. Data is facts a computer can write down.
beats.caption: Tastes and feelings? Not data!

beats.vo: Here's Meena Ma'am. She wrote everyone's marks on little paper slips, and stuffed them all into her bag.
beats.caption: Marks on loose slips, stuffed in a bag

beats.vo: Then the principal asks, what did Rohan get in maths? Oh no! Meena Ma'am digs, and digs, and digs. It takes forever!
beats.caption: "What did Rohan get?" Dig, dig, dig…

beats.vo: Now look at a register. All the names are in A B C order, with the marks right beside them. Go to R, and there's Rohan. Found in a flash!
beats.caption: Register: names in ABC order, marks beside

beats.vo: Computers keep data just like that register. Super tidy, organised lists. That's why your game finds your score faster than a blink.
beats.caption: Computers keep tidy lists → find data fast

beats.vo: Let's try it. Which list makes it easier to find Kavya's score? List A, with scores scribbled anywhere? Or list B, with names in A B C order and scores beside them? Pause, and pick.
beats.caption: List A or List B? Which is quicker?

beats.vo: List B! Go down to K, and there's Kavya, with forty five points. A tidy list is much faster to search than a messy pile.
beats.caption: List B! Tidy lists are quick to search

beats.vo: Now, here's something really important. Some data is okay to share. But some data must stay private.
beats.caption: Some data is public. Some is private.

beats.vo: Public data is fine to share. Like your favourite colour, your favourite cricket team, or a cartoon you like.
beats.caption: Public: favourite colour, team, cartoon

beats.vo: Private data is only for you, and the grown-ups you trust. Your home address. Your phone number. Your birthday. And your passwords.
beats.caption: Private: address, phone, birthday, password

beats.vo: Why keep it private? Remember being safe online? A stranger could use your address to find you, or use your birthday to trick you.
beats.caption: Strangers could find you or trick you

beats.vo: So who can you tell? Only trusted adults. Like mum, dad, or your teacher.
beats.caption: Share only with trusted adults

beats.vo: Let's sort! Favourite colour. Home address. Phone number. Favourite cricket team. Which ones are private? Think about it.
beats.caption: Public or private? Sort them!

beats.vo: Home address and phone number are private. Favourite colour and cricket team are public. And remember, a phone number isn't just a number. Never post it online!
beats.caption: Address & phone: private. Colour & team: public

beats.vo: Uh-oh. You're playing a game, and a pop-up appears. Win a prize! Just type your birthday and your school name. What should you do?
beats.caption: Pop-up: "Type your birthday to win!"

beats.vo: Don't share it! Close it, and tell a trusted adult. Your birthday and school name are private, and a real prize never needs them.
beats.caption: Don't share. Tell a trusted adult!

beats.vo: One more. Your class makes a web page that everyone can see. The class name, and the sports day date? Sure. But parents' phone numbers? No way! They stay private.
beats.caption: Class web page: no phone numbers!

beats.vo: Okay champ, practice check time, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: Is your birthday public data, or private data? And who should you tell? Pause the video, and think.
beats.caption: Birthday: public or private? Who to tell?

beats.vo: It's private! You can tell people you trust, like your family, or your teacher. But never strangers online. Did you get it? Brilliant!
beats.caption: Private! Tell family or teacher only

beats.vo: Let's remember what we learned. Data is facts a computer stores, like names, scores, and photos.
beats.caption: Data = facts: names, scores, photos

beats.vo: Tidy lists are much easier to search than a messy pile.
beats.caption: Tidy lists beat messy piles

beats.vo: Private data, like your address and birthday, stays private.
beats.caption: Private data stays private

beats.vo: And you share private data only with trusted adults.
beats.caption: Share only with trusted adults

beats.vo: Chapter four, done! Next up is the big one. Your capstone, where you design your very own app!
beats.caption: Chapter 4 done! Next: your capstone

beats.vo: But first, tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this, champ!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
